title: Pasta carbonara
description: Spaghetti with crisp bacon, egg yolks and parmesan, made creamy with a splash of pasta water. No cream needed.
steps: Bring a large pot of water with the salt to the boil. Cut the bacon into small strips and grate the parmesan finely.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs in a bowl with the parmesan and the black pepper until smooth. Leave the bowl near the stove.
steps.tip: Take the eggs out of the fridge early if you can. Room-temperature eggs are less likely to scramble.

steps.text: Put the bacon in a large cold frying pan without oil and set it on medium heat. Fry for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and crisp. Turn off the heat and leave the bacon and its fat in the pan.
steps.tip: The fat that melts out is part of the sauce, so do not pour it away.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Before you drain it, scoop out a mug of the pasta water.

steps: Drain the spaghetti and tip it straight into the pan with the bacon, off the heat. Toss well so it gets coated in the fat.

steps.text: Wait a moment until the pan has stopped sizzling. Pour in the egg mix with a splash of pasta water and toss quickly for 1 to 2 minutes until it turns into a glossy, creamy sauce.
steps.tip: Runny? Keep tossing: the heat of the pasta thickens it. Starting to look grainy? Add a splash more pasta water right away, the egg is beginning to scramble.

steps.text: Serve straight away with extra pepper on top.
steps.tip: Carbonara does not wait. The sauce sets as it cools.

title: Egg fried rice with peas
description: Day-old rice fried hot with eggs, peas, carrot and spring onion. The best way to use leftover rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok until very hot. Stir-fry the diced carrot and garlic for 2 minutes, then the peas.
Push everything aside, scramble the beaten eggs in the space, then mix in.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry 4 minutes, pressing it against the pan.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and toss with the spring onion.

title: Tuna and tomato pasta
description: A store-cupboard pasta with canned tuna, tomatoes, capers and olives. On the table in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook the pasta. Warm the garlic and chili in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, capers and olives and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the drained tuna and heat through.
Toss with the pasta and parsley.

title: Bean and cheese quesadillas
description: Crisp tortillas filled with mashed beans, corn, pepper and melted cheese, with a quick tomato salsa.

steps.text: Drain and rinse the beans and drain the sweetcorn. Mash the beans with the cumin and a pinch of salt using a fork until mostly smooth. Dice the pepper and grate the cheese.
steps.tip: A little texture is fine. The mashed beans hold everything together.

steps.text: Spread the beans over one half of each tortilla. Top with sweetcorn, pepper and cheese, then fold the other half over and press gently.
steps.tip: Keep the filling a finger's width from the edge so the cheese does not leak into the pan.

steps: Make the salsa salad: chop the tomatoes and onion finely and mix with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Shred the lettuce.

steps.text: Heat a large dry frying pan on medium. Cook the quesadillas two at a time for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp underneath.
steps.tip: No oil needed. Press with a spatula so the filling sticks together as the cheese melts.

steps: Flip them carefully with a wide spatula and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese has melted. Keep the cooked ones warm under a clean towel while you do the rest.
Cut each quesadilla into wedges and serve with the tomato salsa and lettuce.

title: Chicken fajita wraps
description: Sizzling spiced chicken with peppers and onions in warm tortillas with sour cream and salsa.

steps.text: Slice the chicken into thin strips. Cut the peppers and onion into strips of the same thickness.
steps.tip: Strips of the same size cook in the same time.

steps: In a large bowl mix the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt and oil. Add the chicken and vegetables and toss until everything is coated.

steps.text: Heat a large frying pan on high until very hot. Add half the mixture in one layer and fry for 5 minutes, stirring only every minute or so, until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are charred at the edges. Repeat with the rest.
steps.tip: A crowded pan steams instead of charring, so cook in two batches. The chicken is done when there is no pink inside.

steps: Squeeze the lemon over the filling. Warm the tortillas for a few seconds on each side in a dry pan.
Spread each tortilla with sour cream, add the filling and a spoon of salsa, roll up and eat.

title: Garlic prawn linguine
description: Prawns tossed with garlic, chili, lemon and parsley through linguine. Feels special, takes 20 minutes.

steps.text: If the prawns are frozen, thaw them in a bowl of cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and pat them dry.
steps.tip: Dry prawns fry instead of boiling in their own water.

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Slice the garlic thinly, halve the tomatoes and chop the parsley.

steps.text: Cook the linguine until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Before you drain it, scoop out a mug of the pasta water.

steps: Meanwhile put the olive oil, garlic and chili flakes in a large cold frying pan and warm on medium-low for 3 minutes, until the garlic is just golden.

steps.text: Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, turning once, until they are pink and curled.
steps.tip: Prawns go rubbery when overcooked. Take them off as soon as they are pink all over and shaped like a C. An O shape means overcooked.

steps: Add the tomatoes, the lemon juice and a ladle of pasta water and let it bubble for 1 minute.
Add the drained linguine and the parsley and toss for 1 minute until the pasta is coated in the glossy sauce. Serve straight away.

title: Pad Thai-style noodles
description: Rice noodles with egg, tofu, crunchy cabbage and peanuts in a sweet, sour and salty sauce.
steps: Soak or cook the noodles as the packet says. Mix the soy, ketchup, sugar and lime juice.
Fry the cubed tofu in the oil until golden, push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the shredded cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes, then the noodles and sauce. Toss until coated.
Serve with chopped peanuts and spring onion.

title: Quick chicken ramen
description: A fast noodle soup with ginger and soy broth, sliced chicken, soft-boiled egg, spinach and spring onion.
steps: Simmer 1.5 litres of water with the stock cube, sliced ginger, garlic and soy for 10 minutes. Poach the chicken in it for 10 minutes, then slice.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Add the sliced mushrooms and noodles to the broth and cook as the noodle packet says. Stir in the spinach.
Serve in bowls with the chicken, halved eggs, spring onion and a few drops of sesame oil.

title: Gnocchi with tomato and mozzarella
description: Pan-fried gnocchi in a quick tomato and basil sauce with melting mozzarella. Kids love it.
steps: Chop the garlic. Drain the mozzarella and tear it into pieces. Grate the parmesan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan with a lid on medium-high. Add the gnocchi straight from the packet in one layer and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, turning now and then, until golden and crisp outside.
steps.tip: Do not boil them first: packet gnocchi fry well as they are. Fry in two batches if they do not fit in one layer.

steps: Add the garlic and stir for a few seconds, then pour in the passata and add the basil, spinach and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until the spinach has wilted.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover with the lid and cook on low for 3 minutes until melted.
Serve with the parmesan grated over the top.

title: Spaghetti aglio e olio with spinach and egg
description: Garlic, olive oil and chili spaghetti with wilted spinach and a fried egg on top. Fifteen minutes.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water with the salt to the boil. Peel the garlic and slice it as thinly as you can. Wash the spinach and grate the parmesan.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water, stir so it does not stick together, and cook until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Before you drain it, keep a mug of the pasta water. You need it for the sauce.

steps.text: Meanwhile put {4 tbsp} of the olive oil, the garlic and the chili flakes in a large cold frying pan. Warm on low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the garlic is pale golden.
steps.tip: Go slowly: the garlic should sizzle gently, not fry hard. If the edges start to turn brown, take the pan off the heat at once.

steps.text: Add the spinach to the garlic oil a handful at a time and stir until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Take the pan off the heat.
In a second pan, heat the rest of the oil on medium and fry the eggs for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
steps.tip: If the whites on top stay clear and wobbly, put a lid on the pan for the last moment.

steps.text: Drain the spaghetti and add it to the garlic and spinach with a good splash of the pasta water and half the parmesan. Toss over low heat for 1 minute until glossy.
steps.tip: The oil, water and cheese make a light sauce that coats the pasta. Add more pasta water if it looks dry or oily.

steps.text: Divide between plates, put an egg on top of each and sprinkle with the rest of the parmesan.
steps.tip: Break the yolk over the pasta as you eat. It becomes part of the sauce.

title: 15-minute chickpea and spinach curry
description: Chickpeas and spinach in a quick coconut tomato curry, served with flatbread or rice.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the oil in a large pan on medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.

steps.text: Add the garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
steps.tip: If the spices start sticking, add a spoon of the coconut milk.

steps.text: Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk, add the chickpeas and salt and bring to a bubble. Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
steps.tip: Shake the coconut milk can well before opening, because the cream separates from the liquid.

steps: Meanwhile warm the flatbreads for a few seconds on each side in a dry pan.
Stir the spinach into the curry a handful at a time until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Taste, add salt if needed and serve with the flatbread.

title: Couscous salad with feta and chickpeas
description: Lemony couscous with chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, roasted peppers, feta and parsley. Good for lunch boxes.
steps: Pour 300 ml boiling water over the couscous with the salt, cover for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber, tomato and peppers and chop the parsley.
Mix everything with the drained chickpeas, lemon juice and oil.
Crumble the feta over the top.

title: Turkey and pepper wraps with yogurt
description: Strips of turkey breast fried with peppers and paprika, wrapped with lettuce and garlic yogurt.
steps: Slice the turkey, peppers and onion into strips. Toss with paprika and salt.
Fry in the oil on high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with the crushed garlic.
Fill the warm tortillas with lettuce, turkey and peppers and a spoon of yogurt.

title: Pan-fried salmon with lemon couscous
description: Crisp-skinned salmon with herby lemon couscous and garlicky spinach. Ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Boil a kettle. Chop the parsley, slice the garlic and cut the lemon in half. Take the salmon out of the fridge.

steps.text: Put the couscous in a bowl with half the salt and {1 tbsp} of the olive oil. Pour over {300 ml} boiling water, cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Too much water makes couscous mushy, so measure it.

steps: Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper and sprinkle it with most of the rest of the salt.

steps.text: Heat {1 tbsp} oil in a frying pan on medium-high. Lay the salmon in skin side down, press gently for a few seconds, then fry for 5 minutes without moving it.
steps.tip: The skin is ready when it lets go of the pan by itself and the colour has turned pale two thirds of the way up the side.

steps.text: Turn the salmon and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, then move it to a plate.
steps.tip: Done when it flakes when pressed but is still a little glossy in the middle. Overcooked salmon gets dry.

steps: In the same pan, heat the rest of the oil on medium. Add the garlic for a few seconds, then the spinach with a pinch of salt, and stir until it wilts, about 2 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir in the parsley and the juice of half the lemon. Serve with the salmon and spinach, and the other lemon half cut into wedges.

title: Ćevapi in flatbread with ajvar and onion
description: Grilled ćevapi in warm lepinja with chopped onion, ajvar and a fresh cabbage and tomato salad.
steps: Grill or pan-fry the ćevapi for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the flatbread on the grill or in the pan with the meat juices.
Shred the cabbage, slice the tomatoes and dress with vinegar, oil and a pinch of salt.
Fill the bread with ćevapi, chopped onion and ajvar and serve with the salad.

title: Cheese and herb omelette with salad
description: Fluffy omelettes with grated cheese and herbs, served with tomato salad and bread. Ten minutes per pan.
steps: Make the salad first: slice the tomatoes and cucumber, arrange them on two plates and drizzle with the olive oil and a pinch of the salt. Grate the cheese and chop the parsley.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the rest of the salt and the parsley and beat with a fork until no streaks of white are left.

steps.text: Heat a small non-stick frying pan on medium. Add half the butter and wait until it foams.
steps.tip: When the foam starts to settle the pan is hot enough. If the butter turns brown, lift the pan off the heat for a moment.

steps.text: Pour in half the egg. Let it sit for a few seconds, then stir gently with a spatula, pulling the set edges into the middle, for about 1 minute.
steps.tip: Stop stirring while the top still looks a little wet and creamy. It keeps cooking on the plate.

steps: Scatter half the cheese over the omelette and leave it a few seconds to start melting. Fold it in half and slide it onto a plate next to the salad.

steps.text: Make the second omelette the same way with the rest of the butter, egg and cheese. Serve with the bread.
steps.tip: Keep the first omelette warm under an upturned bowl while you make the second.

title: Halloumi and roasted pepper flatbreads
description: Golden grilled halloumi with roasted peppers, hummus and salad in warm flatbread.
steps: Slice the halloumi and dry-fry 2 minutes a side until golden.
Warm the flatbreads.
Spread with hummus and fill with lettuce, sliced tomato, peppers and halloumi.
Squeeze over a little lemon and roll up.

title: Tortellini with peas and ham
description: Cheese tortellini in a light cream sauce with peas, ham and parmesan. Ten minutes from start to plate.
steps: Cook the tortellini as the packet says, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Warm the diced ham in a pan, add the cream and pepper and bubble 2 minutes.
Toss with the drained tortellini and peas.
Serve with parmesan.

title: Tuna and white bean salad
description: No-cook salad of tuna, beans, red onion, tomatoes and parsley with a mustard dressing. Bread on the side.

steps.text: Slice the onion as thinly as you can. Put it in a large bowl with the vinegar and a pinch of salt, mix and leave for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: The vinegar softens the sharp taste of raw onion and turns red onion bright pink.

steps: Meanwhile drain and rinse the beans, drain the tuna and chop the tomatoes and parsley.
Whisk the mustard and olive oil into the vinegar and onion in the bowl to make the dressing.
Add the beans, tomatoes and parsley and toss gently. Add the tuna in big flakes and fold it in carefully so it does not break up too much. Taste and add salt if needed.

steps.text: Serve with bread.
steps.tip: It makes a good lunch the next day. Keep it in the fridge, and if you can, add the tomatoes just before eating.

title: Penne arrabbiata with chickpeas
description: Fiery tomato and garlic penne made more filling with chickpeas. Vegan and very cheap.

steps.text: Fill a large pot with about {3000 ml} water, add the salt, cover and bring to the boil. Meanwhile slice the garlic thinly, drain and rinse the chickpeas and chop the parsley.
steps.tip: The water should taste lightly salty. It is the only chance to season the pasta itself.

steps.text: Put the olive oil, garlic and chili flakes in a large cold frying pan, then set it on medium-low heat. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the garlic sizzles gently and turns pale gold.
steps.tip: Starting in a cold pan stops the garlic burning. Brown garlic tastes bitter, so lift the pan off the heat if it colours too fast.

steps.text: Pour in the canned tomatoes, crush any big pieces with a spoon and bring to a bubble. Simmer on medium-low for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
steps.tip: It is thick enough when a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a gap that fills slowly.

steps.text: While the sauce simmers, add the penne to the boiling water and stir once. Cook it until al dente, a little less than the packet says, stirring a couple of times.
steps.tip: Al dente means it still has a slight bite in the middle. It finishes cooking in the sauce.

steps.text: Add the chickpeas to the sauce and let them heat through for 3 minutes. Taste and add a pinch of salt if it needs it.

Scoop out a mug of the pasta water, then drain the penne. Tip it into the sauce with a splash of the pasta water and toss over the heat for 1 minute until every piece is coated. Scatter with the parsley and serve.
steps.tip: The starchy pasta water helps the sauce cling to the pasta. Add more a little at a time if it looks dry.
